nodes.name: Challenges and Strategies for Analyzing Urban Flood Resilience Using Earth Observation Data
nodes.venue: GeoHorizons
nodes.abstract: Urban flood resilience has become a critical research focus as cities face increasing flood risks due to climate change, rapid urbanization, and population growth. Earth Observation (EO) technologies support flood resilience by providing essential information across flood preparedness, response, recovery, and adaptation. However, translating EO data into meaningful indicators of urban resilience remains challenging due to issues such as data gaps, classification uncertainties, and difficulties integrating EO data with socio-economic factors. This chapter examines the potential of EO data for urban flood resilience, addressing key challenges in data availability, quality, and processing. As part of this analysis, we present a preliminary assessment of Sentinel-1's temporal coverage of flood events recorded in the EM-DAT database between 2017 and 2024, revealing substantial gaps in acquisition timing and regional coverage, particularly across Africa and South America, that constrain its ability to capture peak flood extents. Building on these findings, the chapter highlights emerging strategies for addressing these limitations, including multi-source data integration, AI-assisted analysis, and stronger links between EO observations and socioeconomic information. Ultimately, advancing urban flood resilience requires interdisciplinary frameworks that combine EO data with social, economic, and institutional knowledge to support more effective and equitable resilience planning.

Towards a Common Understanding in Transport Using a Living Glossary: A Multiperspective Approach to Multimodal Terminology
nodes.venue: Lecture Notes in Mobility Re-Generation in Transport
nodes.abstract: Abstract Enhancing integration across transport modes is a priority of European transport policy. This requires not only technical and operational alignment but also a shared conceptual framework – which is often obstructed by fragmented terminologies and divergent interpretations of the same terms. This paper presents the development of a Living Multimodality Glossary as part of the SIGN-AIR project, designed to address this semantic fragmentation. SIGN-AIR will develop a digital platform enabling Transport Service Providers to collaborate via Smart Contracts and Data Sharing Agreements, based on standardised procedures and harmonised terminology. The SIGN-AIR glossary, beyond being a reference, functions as an instrument of mutual understanding, supporting legal agreements, operational coordination, compliance with required data standards and interoperability across transport domains. The glossary is constructed through a multiperspective methodology that merges desk research and top-down sources (standards, EU regulations) with bottom-up refinements drawn from real-world use cases and experts’ discourse. The process revealed the definitional instability of many terms and definitions as well as the need for context-sensitive interpretations. In all language use, meanings evolve over time – requiring the glossary to remain dynamic and adaptable.

Self-supervised Detection of Harsh Cornering Events at Scale Using Smartphone Sensor Data
nodes.venue: Lecture Notes in Mobility Re-Generation in Transport
nodes.abstract: Abstract This study presents a self-supervised framework for detecting harsh cornering events using smartphone telematics under real-world deployment conditions. GPS-derived trajectory features, orientation-invariant inertial magnitudes, and OpenStreetMap validation are combined to robustly identify candidate turns despite arbitrary device placement and sensor noise. High-confidence pseudo-labels are generated via ensemble anomaly detection, enabling supervised classifiers to learn without manual annotation. Among four evaluated models, a multi-layer perceptron achieved the best performance, and its latent embeddings revealed clear separation between harsh and normal cornering. The results demonstrate that consumer-grade smartphones can reliably capture lateral risky maneuvers at scale, extending prior work focused mainly on longitudinal events such as hard braking. This approach offers a scalable foundation for applications in driver risk assessment, insurance telematics, fleet management, and urban safety planning.

nodes.name: Measuring the Urban–Peri-Urban Mobility Divide Through the Sustainable Mobility Readiness Index
nodes.venue: Lecture Notes in Mobility Re-Generation in Transport
nodes.abstract: Abstract Metropolitan areas face mounting challenges from urbanization, technological disruption, and evolving mobility and logistics demands. Addressing these pressures requires integrated strategies for infrastructure planning, multimodal operations, and resilient development. This study introduces the Sustainable Mobility Readiness Index (SMRI), a decision-support framework designed to assess the preparedness of metropolitan areas for inclusive, innovation-driven, MaaS-enabled, and climate-resilient transport systems. The SMRI evaluates 26 global metropolitan areas—including 7 from Europe, 8 from Asia, 5 from North America, 3 from South America, 2 from Africa, and 1 from Oceania—using 64 indicators across six dimensions: transport supply, transport demand, innovation, policy, finance, and environment-energy. The methodology combines expert-informed weighting, normalization, and sensitivity analysis, capturing both passenger and freight mobility to reflect integrated infrastructure and logistics performance. It also compares urban with peri-urban zones, highlighting spatial inequalities in access, services, and investment. Results show considerable variation in readiness. The top three cities—London, Helsinki, Amsterdam—are all in Europe, reflecting strong policy leadership and sustainability integration. Asian cities also perform above average, particularly in digitalization and multimodal services. North American cities rank moderately, shaped by slower adoption of sustainability-oriented policies. Cities in South America and Africa rank lowest, underscoring persistent infrastructure and investment deficits.

nodes.name: From Metro to Multimodal Mobility Hub: Transforming Thessaloniki’s West Centre for Climate Neutrality
nodes.venue: Lecture Notes in Mobility Re-Generation in Transport
nodes.abstract: Abstract Following the goal of achieving climate neutrality and accelerating the transition of European cities through innovation and digitization, Thessaloniki was awarded with the relevant EU Mission label. As part of its commitment to the NetZeroCities Pilot Programme, the ReGenWesT project builds on one of the Climate City Contract’s emblematic interventions for the creation of climate neutral districts. This paper focuses on pilot actions designed to enhance sustainable urban mobility in the city’s West Centre. The recent metro launch presents a unique opportunity to improve the safety and accessibility of mobility nodes, reduce pollution, and promote sustainable travel, core objectives of the European Green Deal. The methodology outlines how to create secure walking and cycling routes for diverse user groups through GIS mapping, participatory co-design, and on-site pilots. These actions aim to demonstrate the validity of the proposed design and establish a community based, data-driven plan for climate-neutral urban renewal.

nodes.name: Digital Representation of Station Environments for Enhanced Public Transport Routing
nodes.venue: Lecture Notes in Mobility Re-Generation in Transport
nodes.abstract: Abstract Public transport applications typically provide accurate information on stops and departure times. However, their performance decreases significantly in complex station environments where multiple levels and transport modes intersect. This limitation is primarily caused by the lack of detailed spatial data on station interiors. This paper addresses this gap by integrating detailed pedestrian networks within station environments into Austria’s Graph Integration Platform (GIP), the national reference system for transport infrastructure. The approach is based on a standardized modelling framework that combines construction plans, orthophotos and on-site inspections, supported by a structured digitization workflow and coordinated data governance across multiple stakeholders. The resulting data extends existing transport graphs by incorporating indoor pathways, vertical connections (e.g. stairs, escalators, elevators) and conditional attributes such as access restrictions and temporal constraints. This enables seamless multimodal routing across outdoor and indoor environments and improves the accuracy of walking time estimation and accessibility-aware routing. A qualitative comparison with existing routing solutions demonstrates that the integration of detailed station models leads to more realistic route geometries and better representation of complex station layouts. The approach is initially applied to major multimodal hubs in Vienna and extended to stations across Austria. Overall, the approach presents a transferable framework for digitizing station environments which contributes to more precise, accessible and user-oriented journey planning and enhances digital public infrastructure for both public-sector and private service providers.

Cross‐device and cross‐modal arc detection: transfer learning between EAST visible and WEST infrared diagnostics
nodes.venue: Nuclear Fusion
nodes.abstract: Abstract This work presents an engineering-oriented data processing and model training pipeline for Experimental Advanced Superconducting Tokamak (EAST) visible and (W) Environment in Steady-state Tokamak (WEST) infrared data, enabling a systematic study of cross-device and cross-modal electric arc detection. A lightweight convolutional neural network is adopted as a cross-device arc detection model, and joint training and transfer learning experiments are conducted on EAST visible (VIS) and WEST infrared (IR) data. Single‐modality baselines are first trained on EAST and WEST, then evaluated zero‐shot on the opposite device, followed by a comparison of frozen‐backbone and fine‐tuned transfer for VIS → IR and IR → VIS. The results show that models trained from scratch on each diagnostic channel already achieve high precision and recall for arc detection, whereas direct zero-shot cross-modal transfer drives the arc recall on the opposite domain almost to zero. In contrast, starting from the single-modality baselines and modestly fine tuning higher convolutional layers and the classification head on the target domain can significantly restore-cross device, cross-modal detection performance, with positive class precision and recall approaching or even surpassing the single-domain baselines. Class activation map analysis further indicates that, under fine-tuned and joint training configurations, the models consistently focus on the antenna, the arc, and its surrounding scattering region, supporting physically meaningful explanations and suggesting that cross-device, cross-modal training can capture arc related structures that generalize across devices while providing a lightweight, scalable route to reusing imaging-based diagnostic knowledge with reduced annotation and retuning effort. Given that machine protection is safety-critical and that imaging diagnostics are never identical across devices, the transferability demonstrated in this work is directly relevant to equipping next-generation tokamaks such as ITER and BEST with a reliable arc-detection capability before a large native training set becomes available. On a newly commissioned device, arc events are rare, sporadic and safety-relevant, so deferring detection until a sufficiently large native training corpus has accumulated would leave the machine unprotected during the early operational phase, when limited operating experience makes the associated risks most difficult to characterize; cross-machine and cross-modal transfer instead enables a new device to inherit a usable detection capability from the outset. Accordingly, the present work is intended not merely as a benchmark of cross-domain accuracy, but as evidence that scalable, transferable arc monitoring can constitute a machine-protection layer of future fusion reactors.

DLS-Extended: a reduced model to assess the impact of impurity radiation location on optimal magnetic geometry choices for the STEP divertor
nodes.venue: Nuclear Fusion
nodes.abstract: Abstract Alternative Divertor Configurations (ADCs) often make use of high total flux expansion ( f R ) and connection length ( L ∥ ) to improve the access to and the controllability of detachment, a regime vitally important for reactor-class tokamaks such as the Spherical Tokamak for Energy Production (STEP). Achieving detachment on such high-power devices is enabled through radiation from seeded impurity species such as argon and neon, which can lead to radiative losses throughout the flux tube, altering the impact of magnetic geometry on detachment. The detachment location sensitivity (DLS) model analytically predicts detachment access and sensitivity based on upstream conditions, the magnetic geometry and seeded impurity radiation. It assumes the radiation region to have no spatial extent. In this work, we relax this assumption and introduce DLS-Extended, a new reduced 1D model which can capture the effects of the spatial distribution of impurity radiation along the field line. The prediction of radiation extent was verified against SOLPS-ITER simulations of an initial STEP design with a good match. DLS-Extended predicts that the radiation extent found in STEP weakens the detachment access benefit of f R and strengthens the benefit of L ∥ , while the detachment stability of the inner and outer legs is increased and decreased, respectively. This is due to a number of novel radiation-driven effects and has implications for the optimum strike point position in reactor-scale devices. These findings highlight the need for more experimental studies in the presence of broad-radiating impurities. DLS-Extended is distributed under the LGPL-3 open source license and is publicly available on GitHub.

nodes.name: Learning and Shape Analysis of Image Manifolds of Three-Dimensional Objects
nodes.venue: SIAM Journal on Imaging Sciences
nodes.abstract: Abstract. Despite high-dimensionality of images, the sets of images of three-dimensional objects have long been hypothesized to form low-dimensional manifolds, a notion expressed as the so-called manifold hypothesis. What is the nature of such manifolds? How do their geometries vary across objects and object classes? Answering these questions can provide key insights into explaining and advancing the success of machine learning algorithms in computer vision. This paper investigates dual tasks—learning and analyzing shapes of image manifolds—by revisiting a classical problem of manifold learning but from a novel geometrical perspective. It uses geometry-preserving transformations to map the pose manifolds, sets of images formed by rotating three-dimensional objects, to low-dimensional latent spaces. The low-dimensionality of latent spaces facilitates estimation and analysis of these pose manifolds using training data. This paper compares shapes of these manifolds in latent spaces, or latent manifolds, of different three-dimensional objects, using Kendall’s shape analysis, i.e., modulo rigid motions and global scaling. Interestingly, latent manifolds for objects from the same class are frequently similar in geometries. We demonstrate the use of latent geometries to simplify several image processing tasks, such as image interpolations via geodesics, image denoising via manifold projections, and image classification using distances to manifolds.

nodes.name: MILES++: A Generalizable Clustering-Based Ensemble Framework for Multiclass Imbalanced Learning
nodes.venue: ACM Transactions on Intelligent Systems and Technology
nodes.abstract: Imbalanced multiclass learning remains challenging due to skewed class distributions, class overlap, and heterogeneous within-class structure. We revisit the Multiclass Imbalance Learning in Ensembles through Selective Sampling (MILES) framework and study two clustering-based variants: MILES \({}^{k}\) , which uses \( k \) -means with an SSE-based heuristic for selecting the number of clusters, and MILES \({}^{FF}\) , which uses FarthestFirst to explore an alternative centroid-based partitioning strategy. Both variants combine clustering-guided selective sampling with resampling to construct diverse and more balanced training subsets, improving representation of difficult classes while preserving local decision structure. We evaluate MILES on eight real-world multiclass datasets spanning different imbalance regimes, overlap levels, and feature complexities. Across these experiments, MILES is consistently competitive in Multiclass Area Under the Curve ( \(MAUC\) ) and achieves its strongest gains in Macro-F1, with statistically significant improvements over several strong ensemble baselines. MILES also achieves strong Micro-F1 on multiple datasets, while its performance on Geometric Mean ( \( G \) -mean) is competitive but more dataset-dependent. Class-wise analysis further shows that the improvement arises from better recovery of hard classes and systematic reduction of dominant baseline confusion patterns, especially on Page and Satellite, while Hyperspectral highlights a limitation case where high dimensionality and stronger overlap reduce the benefits of centroid-based selective sampling. A glaciology case study on glacier algae prediction further demonstrates the practical utility of the framework. Overall, the results position MILES as a robust and generalizable alternative to conventional boosting, bagging, and cost-sensitive ensembles for multiclass imbalanced learning.

A hybrid predictive maintenance framework using machine learning for RAM study in mining assets
nodes.venue: Journal of Quality in Maintenance Engineering
nodes.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this paper is to develop and validate a hybrid predictive maintenance framework that integrates machine learning–based failure prediction with reliability, availability, and maintainability (RAM) analysis to support proactive maintenance decision-making for asset-intensive mining equipment. Design/methodology/approach The study proposes a Hybrid RAM–predictive maintenance framework hybridRAM–PdM framework that combines short-horizon failure risk classification with quantile-based remaining useful life (RUL) estimation. Supervised tree-ensemble models are employed to predict failure risk at 24, 72, and 168 h, while quantile boosting is used to estimate RUL intervals. Model training is conducted strictly in chronological order to preserve operational realism. Predictive outputs are systematically mapped to RAM indicators, including mean time between failures mean time to repair and asset availability. The framework is validated using three months of real-world Computerized Maintenance Management System data from mining mobile equipment, including dump trucks and load–haul–dump machines. Findings Results indicate that the proposed framework provides useful near-term failure-risk warnings, actionable RUL intervals, and RAM-oriented readiness indicators for maintenance planning. The integration of predictive outputs with observed repair information supports asset-level prioritization and targeted maintenance interventions. However, because the case study is based on a three-month observation window and a limited number of assets, the results should be interpreted as preliminary operational evidence rather than definitive proof of long-term reliability or availability improvement. Research limitations/implications The study is based on a single industrial case study, five assets, and a three-month historical data window containing 25 observed failure events. Future research should evaluate the framework over longer operating periods, larger fleets, additional asset classes, and different industrial sectors. Further work should also incorporate cost-aware threshold optimization and formal validation of the relationship between ML-derived planning indicators and classical RAM quantities. Practical implications The framework enables maintenance practitioners to translate machine-learning predictions into intuitive alerts, RUL-based planning windows, and RAM-oriented readiness indicators. These outputs can support proactive inspection planning, maintenance scheduling, and repair-prioritization decisions, while final deployment should be calibrated using site-specific cost, safety, and production constraints. Originality/value This paper provides a novel contribution by explicitly linking predictive maintenance analytics with RAM performance measures, bridging the gap between data-driven prediction models and practical maintenance engineering decision-making.

Interpretable and backpropagation-free Green Learning for efficient multi-task echocardiographic segmentation and classification
nodes.venue: APSIPA Transactions on Signal and Information Processing
nodes.abstract: Purpose This study develops an interpretable, backpropagation-free multi-task Green Learning (MTGL) framework for automated echocardiographic analysis. It addresses the need for reliable left ventricular (LV) segmentation and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) classification while reducing the parameter burden, energy demand and opacity associated with conventional deep learning (DL) models. The objective is to determine whether a unified feed-forward framework can deliver clinically relevant accuracy, computational efficiency and interpretable feature representations. Design/methodology/approach The framework uses a four-hop, PCA/Saab-based unsupervised VoxelHop encoder followed by a coarse-to-fine XGBoost residual-regression decoder for LV segmentation and a pooled multi-scale XGBoost classifier for three-class LVEF classification. Experiments used the predefined EchoNet-Dynamic training, validation and test partitions. MTGL was evaluated against matched 3D V-Net, 3D U-Net, 3D UNETR and 3D nnU-Net baselines using classification accuracy and balanced accuracy, and Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and intersection over union (IoU). Findings On the EchoNet-Dynamic test set, MTGL achieved 94.3% accuracy for three-class LVEF classification, and 0.912 DSC for LV segmentation, outperforming all compared baselines. It used 1.13 million parameters, versus 10.47–49.08 million for the DL comparators, and showed the lowest measured training energy use and carbon emissions. Hop ablation further showed complementary multi-scale information, with the full feature set yielding the highest classification accuracy. Originality/value Unlike end-to-end backpropagation-based DL methods, MTGL combines an unsupervised linear VoxelHop representation with task-specific XGBoost decoders in a single multi-task echocardiographic pipeline. The PCA/Saab direct current and alternating current feature decomposition enables direct inspection of learned spatial and spatiotemporal signals, linking shallow features to anatomical boundaries and deeper features to global contractile dynamics. The study therefore demonstrates that a compact, interpretable Green Learning system can jointly support LV segmentation and LVEF grouping with strong in-domain performance and lower measured training environmental cost.

nodes.name: SpaRRTa: A Synthetic Benchmark for Evaluating Spatial Intelligence in Visual Foundation Models
nodes.venue: International Journal of Computer Vision
nodes.abstract: Abstract Visual Foundation Models (VFMs), such as DINO and CLIP, excel in semantic understanding of images but exhibit limited spatial reasoning capabilities, which limits their applicability to embodied systems. As a result, recent work has incorporated some 3D tasks (such as depth estimation) into VFM training. However, VFM performance remains inconsistent across other spatial tasks, raising the question of whether these models truly possess spatial awareness or overfit to specific 3D objectives. To address this question, we introduce the Spatial Relation Recognition Task (SpaRRTa) benchmark, which evaluates the ability of VFMs to identify static directional relations between visible objects. Unlike traditional 3D objectives that focus on precise metric prediction (e.g., surface normal estimation), SpaRRTa probes a fundamental capability underpinning more advanced forms of human-like spatial understanding. SpaRRTa generates an arbitrary number of photorealistic images with diverse scenes and fully controllable object arrangements, along with freely accessible spatial annotations. Evaluating a range of state-of-the-art VFMs, we reveal significant disparities in their ability to encode directional spatial relations. Through our analysis, we provide insights into the mechanisms that support or hinder this form of spatial awareness in modern VFMs. We hope that SpaRRTa will serve as a useful tool for guiding the development of future spatially aware visual models. Our project page can be found at https://sparrta.gmum.net/ .

nodes.name: A UAV-based real-time detection system of flowering nectar plants using a lightweight deep learning model
nodes.venue: Precision Agriculture
nodes.abstract: Abstract Purpose Timely knowledge of flowering status and peak blooming periods in transferred areas is crucial for migratory beekeepers to make informed management decisions. Traditional manual field surveys are labor-intensive, time-consuming, and unsuitable for frequent monitoring. Current monitoring approaches using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) rely on offline processing and require complex data analysis by specialists, making them impractical for beekeepers to implement in apicultural settings. Given the short time window for capturing flowering events, especially for species with short florescence periods, an accurate, fast monitoring solution is needed. We developed a UAV-based real-time investigation prototype leveraging edge-intelligence computing for nectar flower detection of Rhus chinensis in complex mountainous field conditions. Methods An improved, high-precision, and lightweight deep learning model based on YOLOv5s was proposed. The model was optimized with acceleration strategies during deployment to reduce inference time. Results Experimental results showed that the proposed model for flower detection achieved a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 89.5 and an inference speed of 56 frames per second (FPS). After applying acceleration strategies during model deployment on the edge computing device, the processing throughput reached 192 FPS with a mAP of 89.2; a 3.1% increase in mAP and approximately a 5.6 times improvement in FPS compared to the original YOLOv5s. Conclusions These results demonstrate that the proposed lightweight model and acceleration strategies effectively balance high accuracy with high-throughput onboard image processing. The developed UAV-edge computing system provides a promising prototype for future efficient nectar flowering status monitoring, with potential applications in smart apiculture.

nodes.name: Physiology‐Informed Layered Sensing for Intelligent Human–Exoskeleton Interaction
nodes.venue: SmartSys
nodes.abstract: ABSTRACT Wearable exoskeletons offer substantial potential to enhance human mobility in everyday environments. However, their translation beyond laboratory environments remains limited by sensing systems that capture movement but not underlying physiology. Here, we introduce a physiology‐layered perception framework for wearable exoskeletons that aligns sensing and inference with the bone–muscle–skin hierarchy to provide task‐specific physiological cues for assistance, effort optimization, and safety co‐monitoring. The framework maps inertial measurement units (IMUs) to skeletal kinematics, surface electromyography (sEMG) to muscular activation, and strain to cutaneous deformation, with real‐time neural decoders tailored to each objective. As a system‐level demonstration of this framework, we implement it in a soft, lightweight smart‐textile platform integrated with a portable ankle exoskeleton (on‐body sensing and electronics weighing < 20 g). Under leave‐one‐subject‐out evaluation on unseen users, the platform achieves accurate ankle joint‐moment estimation (RMSE = 0.13 Nm kg −1 ), real‐time classification of metabolic trends (96.3% accuracy), and sub‐100 ms detection of injury‐related risk (recall = 0.96). This work establishes a physiology‐aligned sensing architecture that reframes exoskeleton perception from motion tracking to real‐time physiological decoding, offering a pathway toward intelligent, adaptive, and personalized wearable robotics.

nodes.name: Memristor‐Based Neuromorphic Computing for Intelligent Sensing and Edge Applications
nodes.venue: Advanced Computing
nodes.abstract: ABSTRACT Memristor‐based neuromorphic computing has emerged as a promising hardware paradigm for energy‐efficient, scalable artificial intelligence edge applications. This review surveys recent progress in memristor‐based neuromorphic computing, in‐memory computing architectures, learning algorithms, and hardware implementations for edge intelligence. Volatile and nonvolatile memristive dynamics are discussed as key mechanisms for emulating biological neurons and synapses, providing foundational building blocks for crossbar‐based hardware neural networks. Moving beyond conventional neural‐network acceleration, this review examines the integration of memristive technologies into edge‐specific applications, focusing on emerging in‐sensor computing, optical in‐memory computing, and multimodal sensing frameworks. Furthermore, we outline the deployment of hardware‐compatible, brain‐inspired algorithms—including artificial, spiking, and recurrent neural networks—and evaluate their physical implementation within memristive architectures. The review also highlights the evolution of memristor‐based hardware from single‐device demonstrations to array‐level accelerators and CMOS‐integrated system‐on‐chip platforms, with the associated hierarchical challenges and solutions. By bridging the gap between individual device physics and full system engineering, this review provides a comprehensive roadmap for developing highly adaptive, low‐latency, and autonomous hardware platforms for the next generation of localized edge intelligence.

nodes.name: Complaint Driven Clinical Guidance and ICD Chapter Suggestion: An AI‐Based Text Classification Tool
nodes.venue: Journal of Evaluation in Clinical Practice
nodes.abstract: ABSTRACT Rationale, Aims and Objectives Accurate routing of patients to appropriate clinical departments is essential for timely diagnosis, effective treatment, and efficient use of hospital resources. However, hospital statistics and feedback from patients and healthcare staff indicate that many patients select clinics that are not appropriate for their presenting complaints. This mismatch unnecessarily occupies appointment slots, limits access to appropriate care, and increases the operational burden on healthcare systems. To address this problem, a complaint‐driven clinical guidance framework was developed to map patient complaints to suitable clinical departments and corresponding International Classification of Diseases (ICD) chapters. Method A 7‐year electronic health record dataset comprising 1,795,645 patient complaints was used to train and evaluate conventional machine learning algorithms and BERT‐based language models. The final classification tasks included 15 clinical departments for department recommendation and 12 ICD chapters for suggestion. Results For clinical department recommendation, Turkish BERT achieved the best performance, with a mean accuracy of 92.02%, precision of 92.91%, and F1‐score of 92.08%. McNemar's test confirmed that its improvement over multilingual BERT‐based alternatives was statistically significant. Error analysis indicated that most department‐level misclassifications occurred between clinically related or symptomatically overlapping departments, including Internal Medicine–Cardiology, Neurosurgery and Physical Therapy, and Cardiovascular Surgery–Cardiology. For ICD chapter suggestion, Turkish BERT achieved the best performance among the evaluated models, with a top‐1 accuracy of 66.7%, top‐3 accuracy of 82.9%, top‐5 accuracy of 85.4%. Conclusion Although exact ICD chapter prediction remained challenging, the substantially higher top‐3 and top‐5 accuracies indicate that the model may be useful for generating ranked candidate ICD chapters. Confusion analysis showed that errors were mainly concentrated between clinically overlapping ICD chapters, particularly neoplasms/blood and immune disorders, endocrine/metabolic diseases, circulatory system diseases, and symptom‐based chapters. These findings suggest that artificial intelligence‐based systems can effectively support clinical department recommendation to improve hospital workflow efficiency, whereas ICD chapter suggestion may serve as a preliminary ranked decision‐support tool.

nodes.name: Research Progress and Clinical Translational Application of Ultrasound Localization Microscopy in Microcirculation Imaging
nodes.venue: Advanced Ultrasound in Diagnosis and Therapy
nodes.abstract: Abstract As an emerging super-resolution ultrasound imaging technology, ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM) breaks the acoustic diffraction limit of conventional ultrasound. By localizing and tracking individual microbubble contrast agents at the sub-wavelength scale, ULM achieves high-precision visualization and quantitative evaluation of micron-level microvascular structures and hemodynamic parameters. Compared with traditional color Doppler flow imaging and contrast-enhanced ultrasound, ULM possesses superior spatial resolution and microcirculation quantification capability, enabling in-depth analysis of microvascular morphological remodeling and functional perfusion abnormalities. This review summarizes the core technical principles, optimized algorithms, and key technical bottlenecks of ULM, including microbubble signal separation, single-bubble localization accuracy, physiological motion artifacts, and prolonged acquisition duration. Furthermore, we comprehensively elaborate the preclinical and clinical application progress of ULM in multiple systems, covering neurovascular, renal, tumor, cardiovascular, endocrine and cardiac microcirculation diseases, with a specific focus on its novel clinical value in identifying vulnerable carotid atherosclerotic plaques. We also discuss the current limitations restricting large-scale clinical translation, standardized protocol establishment, and deep-tissue imaging performance of ULM, noting that the majority of existing human ULM evidence is still at the feasibility stage and large-scale prospective multi-center clinical validations are still needed. Targeting the above-mentioned translational bottlenecks, finally, this review prospects the future development directions of ULM, including artificial intelligence optimization, three-dimensional whole-organ imaging, multi-modal and multi-omics fusion. With continuous technical iteration, ULM is expected to become a novel non-invasive imaging modality for early diagnosis, risk stratification and therapeutic efficacy evaluation of microcirculation-related disorders.

nodes.name: Robust real-time GNSS satellite clock estimation using atomic clock models with anomaly detection and mitigation
nodes.venue: Satellite Navigation
nodes.abstract: Abstract Real-time Precise Point Positioning (RT-PPP) relies heavily on precise Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) satellite clock products. Model-based clock estimation can exploit the improved stability of modern atomic clocks to establish and maintain a stable network timescale. However, conventional clock models cannot adequately handle clock anomalies, such as phase and frequency jumps, which can degrade clock estimation accuracy and compromise filter stability. To address this issue, we propose and validate an anomaly-aware real-time satellite clock estimation framework that integrates atomic clock modeling with anomaly identification, isolation, and recovery within a network solution, thereby limiting the propagation of clock anomalies into the network time reference. To further assess the reliability and practical applicability of the framework, the anomaly-confirmation parameters are systematically evaluated, and the computational efficiency is assessed to verify real-time feasibility. Subsequently, validation using actual GNSS data demonstrates the effective identification and mitigation of phase jumps, frequency jumps, and complex anomalies. Real-time service performance evaluation shows that the method achieves comparable or improved clock accuracy across multiple GNSS constellations, while significantly enhancing timescale stability. The proposed approach therefore provides a more stable and resilient real-time GNSS timescale, thereby supporting high-accuracy timing applications.

nodes.name: Comparative Analysis of Multimodal <scp>GANs</scp> for Cross‐Modal Information Retrieval
nodes.venue: WIREs Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery
nodes.abstract: ABSTRACT Cross‐modal information systems have emerged as an important area of research that enables information retrieval in different modalities such as text, image and audio. Existing Cross‐modal retrieval methods focus on semantic consistency between modalities but rarely consider retrieval effectiveness in generative models. This study investigates the effectiveness of the Multimodal Generative Advertisement Network (MMGAN) in enhancing Cross‐modal Information Retrieval (CMIR) performance. Using benchmark datasets that include various modalities, it conducts a comprehensive analysis of MMGAN against several state‐of‐the‐art models, including traditional Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). The experimental evaluation considers both representation quality and cross‐modal retrieval effectiveness. Controlled unimodal benchmarks are used to examine latent representation quality, whereas MS‐COCO, containing paired image–text samples, serves as the primary benchmark for genuine cross‐modal retrieval. Retrieval performance is assessed using Mean Average Precision (mAP), Precision@K, Recall@K, and NDCG@K for image‐to‐text and text‐to‐image retrieval, while NMI, ARI, and clustering accuracy are employed as supplementary measures of representation and semantic grouping quality. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed MMGAN‐based framework in learning semantically aligned multimodal representations and improving cross‐modal retrieval performance. Furthermore, it analyses the strengths and limitations of MMGAN, informing readers of their potential applications and exploring future research directions in CMIR. It contributes to the advancement of generative models to improve Cross‐modal retrieval systems, emphasizing more efficient and effective information retrieval.

Beyond similarity retrieval: governance fidelity, consistency, and minimality in long-term conversational memory
nodes.venue: International Journal of Data Science and Analytics
nodes.abstract: Abstract Conversational language model systems persist user constraints, preferences, identity, commitments, and assigned roles across turns. The dominant memory architecture stores this alongside ordinary episodic content in a vector index and retrieves the top- k items by similarity to the active query. We argue that this design is structurally inappropriate for the subset of items we call governing facts: facts whose binding force does not depend on their similarity to the current query. We define governance fidelity, the fraction of governing facts that reach the assembled context, and prove a small impossibility result: any retriever that ranks by a type-blind similarity score and returns a bounded top- k can be defeated by an adversarial topical-noise sequence. The remedy is type-conditional retrieval. We instantiate it as Stratified Context Reconstruction (SCR) in Satchel, a typed graph memory. Across 2880 sparse-and-hybrid and 2160 dense retrieval measurements, governance fidelity collapses from 1.0 to below 0.10 by N = 100 adversarial noise pairs for every similarity retriever tested; dense bi-encoders collapse as well, and a follow-up sweep over larger encoders (bge-large, e5-large) and a cross-encoder reranker confirm that the collapse is intrinsic to similarity ranking and is not avoided by stronger or larger encoders, which postpone but do not prevent it. SCR holds fidelity at 1.0 by construction (Cohen’s d = 1.06, p ≈ 2.6 + 10⁻ 25 ). We further show that type-conditional retrieval alone is insufficient once governing facts are revised over time: we prove a second impossibility—governance consistency cannot be guaranteed by any conflict-blind retriever, and the error grows linearly in revision depth—and give SCR-T, a temporally stratified, supersession-resolved retriever that attains both completeness and consistency by construction. A revision-depth benchmark confirms the prediction: naive SCR returns up to fifteen stale superseded facts per query and its governance minimality—the precision of the governing block—decays to 0.25, while SCR-T returns none and holds fidelity, consistency, and minimality jointly at 1.0. We frame these three as governance invariants against which conversational memory should be evaluated, alongside traceability as a structural property of typed memory. On four small open-weight LLMs, SCR improves constraint adherence over a TF-IDF RAG baseline by 17.59 percentage points. A further live-LLM experiment under the paper’s own adversarial noise, with retrieval and prompt formatting separated in a controlled four-arm design, shows that SCR’s downstream advantage is a high-noise phenomenon that grows with noise volume and is not an artefact of formatting.

An intelligent cybersecurity framework for banking systems: integrating neural networks, large language models, and federated learning for anti-money laundering and fraud detection
nodes.venue: Future Business Journal
nodes.abstract: Abstract The fraud of money laundering costs the global financial system USD 800 billion to USD 2 trillion annually, while digital banking contributes to the increasing number and complexity of money laundering transactions. If there are adversarial forces that are constantly adapting their approach to avoid complying with a conventional rule-based compliance program, that isn’t going to work. In this paper, we present a comprehensive, layered cybersecurity framework for banking systems, combining graph neural networks (GNNs), long short-term memory (LSTM) architectures, large language models (LLMs) and federated learning, aimed at tackling anti-money laundering (AML) and transaction fraud detection on a massive scale. The framework is based on the theoretical constructs of agency theory, information asymmetry theory, and routine activity theory and is situated in the context of a formal mathematical model that encodes the temporal dependencies of transactions, the topology of the relationships between transactions, and the semantic context of their behavior. This multistage detection pipeline involves supervised classification, unsupervised anomaly detection, regulatory narration with the assistance of LLM and an explainable-AI (XAI) layer for regulatory transparency. It has been developed and designed to operate in a federated manner, which means that the data can be shared among different institutions without the risk of it being shared with the raw data, thus ensuring data privacy in line with GDPR provisions. Benchmarks with publicly available AML datasets show that the proposed hybrid model outperforms the standalone rule-based model and single-model baseline with an area under the ROC curve (AUROC) of 0.961. The framework gives a hands-on and theory-based guide for intelligent, trustworthy financial crime detection to address regulators, compliance officers and data scientists’ evolving needs.

nodes.name: Beyond classification: a systematic review of advanced predictive methodologies in retinal image analysis
nodes.venue: Research on Biomedical Engineering
nodes.abstract: Abstract Background The retina provides a unique, non-invasive window into the human microvascular and central nervous systems. Recent advancements in deep learning have catalyzed the emergence of “Oculomics” transitioning automated retinal image analysis from localized ophthalmic diagnostics to holistic systemic health assessment. Objective This systematic review synthesizes the state-of-the-art computational pipelines, training paradigms, and explainability frameworks that enable the extraction of predictive systemic biomarkers from retinal imaging. Methods We trace the evolution of methods from traditional pixel-wise classification to complex topology-aware graph representations. We also curated a comprehensive landscape of fundus imaging data sets. We further document the growing practice of aggregating many public data sets into large corpora for pretraining vision–language foundation models. The results are organized into four distinct views to provide a clearer perspective on the field’s development. Results By leveraging multivariate biobanks and advanced Foundation Models, these structural representations demonstrate remarkable accuracy in predicting cardiovascular, renal, and neurodegenerative risks, often rivaling invasive clinical metrics. Crucially, we highlight a methodological mandate for eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) in clinical translation. Techniques such as concept-based interpretability, spatial attention mapping, and human-in-the-loop validation are actively mitigating the algorithmic black box, directly linking predictive risk scores — such as retinal biological age — to clinically verifiable physiological changes. Conclusion Despite persistent challenges related to data set homogeneity, cross-domain generalization, sensitivity to image quality, “residual black-box” modules, scarce longitudinal cohorts, and lack of regulatory standardization frameworks integrating robust graph-based and multimodal architectures with transparent XAI modules, positions automated retinal biomarkers as a transformative “human-in-the-loop” tool for non-invasive, population-level systemic risk stratification.

nodes.name: Damage detection, localization, and sizing in composite structures using modal shape and multi-head convolutional neural network
nodes.venue: Machine Learning for Computational Science and Engineering
nodes.abstract: Abstract Owing to their favorable weight-to-performance characteristics, composite sandwich panels are extensively employed across engineering sectors; however, internal defects often escape identification when relying on conventional, visually-driven inspection routines. This study proposes a data-driven framework combining modal shape, image processing, and a multi-head convolutional neural network (CNN) for automated damage identification, localization, and extent estimation. Damage is numerically modeled by introducing localized regions of reduced stiffness through the insertion of low-stiffness material in the core, skin, or interface layers, enabling realistic representation of structural degradation. The first five non-null vibration mode shapes are transformed into contour images and used as inputs to the proposed architecture. A multi-head CNN processes each vibration mode independently to enhance feature extraction and structural condition classification into four categories: undamaged, core damage, skin damage, and interface damage. Subsequently, a dedicated CNN predicts damage position and geometry based on two spatial coordinates and three shape parameters. Among the evaluated image processing techniques, the residual approach yielded the best performance, achieving F1-scores of 0.99 for core damage and 0.87 for both skin and interface damage. The framework also achieved high localization capability, with an average position error of approximately 4% and maximum relative errors below 5% of the plate dimensions; these localization and sizing results were obtained using the ground-truth damage class to route each sample to its corresponding regression network, and therefore do not reflect the potential propagation of classification errors through the complete classification-routing-regression pipeline. Compared with a previously developed baseline model, the proposed framework reduced the mean absolute error for most geometric parameters, with improvements exceeding 30% in several localization and sizing tasks. Despite challenges in angular orientation prediction, these results demonstrate the potential of the proposed methodology for structural health monitoring of composite sandwich structures.

Intraprocedural echocardiographic guidance in transcatheter mitral valve interventions: from procedure-specific workflows to integrated multimodal platforms
nodes.venue: Journal of Cardiovascular Imaging
nodes.abstract: Abstract Mitral regurgitation (MR) is the most common left-sided valvular heart disease worldwide and carries significant morbidity and mortality when untreated. The expanding use of transcatheter mitral valve interventions (TMVIs), including mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) and transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR), to anatomically complex, high-risk patient populations has substantially increased the demands on intraprocedural echocardiographic guidance. Yet current consensus documents provide modality-level guidance without explicitly formalizing the divergent imaging requirements inherent to these two mechanistically distinct interventions. This state-of-the-art review synthesizes evidence on intraprocedural echocardiographic guidance for TMVIs, integrating current data on 2D and 3D transesophageal echocardiography, real-time multiplanar reconstruction (MPR), echocardiography-fluoroscopy fusion imaging, 3D intracardiac echocardiography, and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted decision-support tools. Two fundamentally distinct imaging paradigms are identified and formalized: a leaflet-level, temporally driven framework for M-TEER and an annular-level, spatially driven framework for TMVR. These paradigms reflect divergent anatomical targets and imaging priorities, with concrete implications for workflow design, operator-echocardiographer communication, and complication avoidance. Real-time MPR serves as the geometric backbone bridging 2D temporal precision with 3D spatial clarity. AI-assisted tools provide a computational guidance layer enhancing spatial consistency and procedural reproducibility while preserving, and not replacing, expert echocardiographic judgment. Effective intraprocedural echocardiographic guidance is objective-driven rather than modality-centric. The modalities described in this review function not as interchangeable alternatives but as complementary layers of a coherent, workflow-integrated architecture. The transition toward integrated, platform-based multimodal guidance defines the trajectory of next-generation TMVI echocardiography, requiring rigorous prospective validation, protocol standardization across device platforms, and training frameworks that reflect the multimodal nature of modern structural practice.

nodes.name: Modern generative large language models in epilepsy care: a scoping review of current applications, challenges, and future directions
nodes.venue: Acta Epileptologica
nodes.abstract: Abstract Modern generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being evaluated in epilepsy-related clinical tasks, but the evidence remains fragmented and their safe clinical role is uncertain. We conducted a scoping review following the PRISMA-ScR framework, searching PubMed, Embase, and the Web of Science Core Collection from inception to May 2026, to map current applications of modern generative LLMs in epilepsy-related clinical contexts and identify their reported benefits, limitations, and research gaps. Eligible studies evaluated generative LLMs or generative foundation models as the primary analytical or assistive engine in clinical or clinically oriented epilepsy tasks; non-generative natural language processing, conventional machine-learning, and signal-modeling studies served as contextual comparators only. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data for descriptive mapping and narrative synthesis. Twenty-four studies were included. Evidence was relatively more developed for text-centered tasks, including information extraction from electronic health records, question answering, and documentation support, while applications in differential diagnosis, presurgical evaluation, prognostic assessment, and patient communication remained early-stage. Across studies, the evidence base was heterogeneous, with frequent reliance on retrospective or simulated designs, single-center data, and limited external validation, alongside persistent concerns about hallucination, bias, model opacity, and workflow integration. Current evidence suggests a limited role for cautious, clinician-supervised use of generative LLMs in selected text-heavy epilepsy tasks, particularly extraction, summarization, documentation support, and patient education, but falls short of justifying independent or routine clinical deployment. Future studies should use narrower task definitions, epilepsy-specific datasets, transparent reporting of model versions and prompt design, external validation, and explicit documentation of clinician verification workflows.

Thinking outside the frame: viewpoint-aware spatial reasoning in large multimodal models
nodes.venue: Visual Intelligence
nodes.abstract: Abstract Large multimodal models (LMMs) have greatly improved cross-modal tasks but continue to struggle with spatial reasoning. In particular, they exhibit a bias toward egocentric reasoning and have limited ability to reframe spatial relations allocentrically, making them unreliable under allocentric viewpoints. In response, we first propose a lightweight viewpoint-aware self-correction strategy with low token overhead that serves as an inductive signal, sensitizing the model to frame-of-reference changes and guiding a corresponding shift in its reasoning trajectory. Second, beyond final-answer accuracy, we introduce a multi-hop spatial reasoning trace that decomposes reasoning into a front-hop object identification stage and a back-hop spatial relation inference stage to expose intermediate reasoning states and assess whether genuine viewpoint transformations occur. Third, we further design robustness-oriented metrics, including hop degradation slope (HDS) and minimality and redundancy of multi-hop reasoning (MRR), to enable a finer-grained analysis of multi-hop reasoning behavior. Finally, we conduct comprehensive quantitative and qualitative evaluations on Spatial-CoT and COMFORT to validate the effectiveness of our approach and provide insights into robustness and failure modes.

nodes.name: Goal-directed synergistic fusion navigation for robust localization under cross-scenario spatial uncertainty
nodes.venue: Satellite Navigation
nodes.abstract: Abstract A goal-directed synergistic fusion navigation framework is essential for enabling accurate and reliable navigation of autonomous unmanned systems across diverse operational scenario environments, especially under challenging conditions such as Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS)-denied and visual-degraded/Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR)-degraded environments. However, it is almost inevitable to encounter spatial uncertainty arising from the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of perceptual information, which may lead to the degradation and the unreliability of navigation. To address this issue, this article proposes a synergistic fusion navigation method against spatial uncertainty inspired by human navigation. Within a unified framework, the system transforms multi-source sensor observations into navigation landmarks, and an online quantitative assessment of sensor availability analysis is performed by analyzing their effective quantity and distribution to define the Degree of Sufficiency (DoS). Based on this, we further design an adaptive state estimation strategy that dynamically adjusts the filtering and optimization processes according to the DoS. To improve the fusion performance, Degree of Observability (DoO)-driven information credibility analysis, opinion dynamics modeling, and factor graph optimization are integrated for the optimal fusion of multi-source navigation information. Real-world experiments show that in complex cross-scenario environments, the proposed method achieves localization Root Mean Square (RMS) errors ranging from 0.32 m to 0.97 m over test trajectories spanning 419.91–1429.80 m. It outperforms State of the Art (SOTA) algorithms and ablation models in both accuracy and reliability.

nodes.name: Beyond unimodal metrics: a multimodal evaluation framework for geo-referenced content on social media
nodes.venue: GeoInformatica
nodes.abstract: Abstract Social media platforms generate large volumes of real-time, geo-referenced content during natural hazards, enabling multimodal topic models to uncover latent themes and their spatial organisation. However, the evaluation of such models typically relies on unimodal metrics, primarily semantic coherence, which overlook spatial structure, temporal dynamics, and the practical usefulness of discovered topics. This paper proposes a multidimensional evaluation framework for disaster-related social media analysis that integrates semantic, spatial, temporal, and operational indicators of topic quality. The framework distinguishes between Utility Information Value (UIV), capturing the informational usefulness of topic representations, and Diagnostic Information Value (DIV), capturing the structural and hazard-consistent validity of spatial and spatio-temporal topic patterns. We examine the framework through a comparative benchmarking analysis of multimodal topic models (MultiGraph and JSTTS) alongside a strong unimodal baseline, using eight geo-referenced datasets from X (Twitter) and Bluesky covering earthquakes, floods, hurricanes, and wildfires under a unified experimental setup. Results show that multimodal models achieve higher actionability (up to 0.75), while the unimodal baseline shows greater semantic diversity (up to 0.99). Spatio-temporal interaction varies across hazards (0.07-0.45), and spatial patterns exhibit hazard-dependent structure. UIV and DIV are strongly correlated (Pearson $$r = 0.89$$ ). However, mean performance remains similar across models (UIV $$\approx$$ 0.49-0.50, DIV $$\approx$$ 0.52-0.53), with no statistically significant differences ( $$p> 0.05$$ ), indicating that performance differences are moderate and dataset-dependent rather than consistently model-driven.

nodes.name: Translating intention: AI-assisted model generation for collaborative human–robot construction
nodes.venue: Construction Robotics
nodes.abstract: Abstract Architectural design has long relied on 2D construction drawings as mediators between design ideation and construction, translating intent into material action. As robots increasingly join humans on building sites, these established communicative practices face epistemic tension: humans interpret drawings through tacit and experiential knowledge, whereas robots require explicit, procedural, and unambiguous instructions. This research investigates how architectural design intent, as represented through drawings, can be effectively communicated to facilitate shared interpretation and collaboration between human and robotic agents. We propose an integrated dual-model approach that distinguishes between what to build (spatial–topological) and how to build it (procedural–topological). Building on this, we develop a speculative framework that automates the generation of these models from construction drawings using multimodal AI, fostering a collaborative human–robot communication in architectural construction. We present initial examples and results of this workflow and discuss their implications for future human–robot collaborative practices.

nodes.name: An integrated framework for GPS flex power analysis: robust detection, automated localization, and spatiotemporal characteristics
nodes.venue: Satellite Navigation
nodes.abstract: Abstract The dynamic redistribution of transmit power by modernized Global Position System (GPS) satellites, known as flex power, significantly enhances anti-jamming capabilities but simultaneously introduces code biases into precise observables, specifically affecting Differential Code Bias (DCB). Notably, the spatial centroids of these flex power zones frequently coincide with regions experiencing complex electromagnetic environments, thereby necessitating robust and reliable monitoring capabilities. However, current monitoring paradigms exhibit critical limitations: existing detection methods suffer from low-gain false alarms and transition-boundary delays, while spatial localization relies entirely on inefficient manual fitting. To address these deficiencies, this study proposes an integrated framework comprising rigorous theoretical modeling, a novel Closed-Loop Flex Power Detection with Sidereal Filtering (CL-FPD-SF) method, and a Greedy-Strategy-Based Adaptive Centroid Fitting Algorithm (GACFA). Experimental results demonstrate the CL-FPD-SF method yields an exceptional average True Positive Rate (TPR) of 0.99997 and a False Positive Rate (FPR) of $$3.6\times {10}^{-6}$$ 3.6 × 10 - 6 . Meanwhile GACFA automates the localization of enhancement centers, effectively replacing traditional manual fitting. Through continuous analysis of global data streams over a five-year period (2020–2025), the proposed framework successfully identified and mapped nine distinct flex power modes, thereby validating the algorithm's robustness and long-term reliability.

nodes.name: Reliable retrieval-augmented feature generation with large language model reasoning
nodes.venue: Knowledge and Information Systems
nodes.abstract: Abstract Feature generation can significantly enhance learning outcomes, particularly for tasks with limited data. An effective way to improve feature generation is to expand the current feature space using existing features and enriching the informational content. However, generating new, interpretable features usually requires domain-specific knowledge on top of the existing features. In this paper, we introduce a Retrieval-Augmented Feature Generation method, RAFG, to generate useful and explainable features specific to domain classification tasks. To increase the interpretability of the generated features, we conduct knowledge retrieval among the existing features in the domain to identify potential feature associations. These associations are expected to help generate useful features. Moreover, we develop a framework based on large language models (LLMs) for feature generation with reasoning to evaluate their semantic relevance, causal alignment, and expected utility for the downstream task. To mitigate the risk of overconfident or unsupported reasoning, we further introduce a counterfactual validation mechanism that compares reasoning-based predictions with observed performance changes. Experiments across several datasets in medical, economic, and geographic domains show that our RAFG method can produce high-quality, meaningful features and significantly improve classification performance compared with baseline methods.

nodes.name: Robust and efficient visual odometry using colored point cloud maps via dual-sparsity and hierarchical optimization
nodes.venue: Satellite Navigation
nodes.abstract: Abstract Reliable localization is fundamental to navigation in GNSS-challenged environments, yet monocular visual odometry (VO) inevitably suffers from drift without global constraints. Point cloud maps can provide global corrections to mitigate this drift. However, existing heterogeneous feature registration methods fail to fully exploit the shared information between vision and point clouds. This limitation results in suboptimal localization accuracy, reduced robustness, and increased computational overhead. To address these issues, we propose a visual odometry system based on colored point cloud maps, which leverages both the global point cloud map as a constraint and the shared modality (color) between the colored point cloud map and the camera to ensure localization accuracy and robustness. The system consists of two main components: sparse colored point cloud construction and visual localization. In the sparse colored point cloud construction module, we introduce a map sparsification strategy that associates visual gradients with point clouds, ensuring that the retained sparse point cloud preserves salient visual gradient information, thereby reducing computational costs. This strategy is further incorporated into the vision-to-map matching stage, forming a “dual-sparsity matching” scheme. In the localization stage, we propose a hierarchical optimization-based iterative Kalman filtering algorithm, which performs multi-level iterative optimization over multi-resolution images to prevent localization from getting trapped in local optima while enhancing accuracy. Experiments on public and self-collected sequences demonstrate significant gains in both accuracy and efficiency. Compared with a representative map-based method (DSL), the proposed approach reduces ATE (RMSE) by $$52\%$$ 52 % – $$95\%$$ 95 % across multiple challenging sequences, with a representative improvement from 1.883 to $$0.152\,\text {m}$$ 0.152 m on R3live_5 ( $$91.92\%$$ 91.92 % reduction). Against the learning-based I2D-Loc++, our method achieves accuracy gains of up to $$76.6\%$$ 76.6 % and maintains robust tracking in extreme cases (e.g., R3live_3/4 ) where I2D-Loc++ and ORB-SLAM3 fail due to visual degradation. Furthermore, the system maintains near real-time efficiency, reducing total processing time by up to $$47.7\%$$ 47.7 % (e.g., from 121.11 to $$63.34\,\text {s}$$ 63.34 s on Whu_1 ). Even under severe geometric degeneracy, our tracker remains robust with an ATE of $$0.076\,\text {m}$$ 0.076 m , whereas geometry-only LiDAR–IMU localization degrades to $$9.23\,\text {m}$$ 9.23 m .

nodes.name: Enhancing sparse multi-view super-resolution with unified multi-plane image spatial representation
nodes.venue: Visual Intelligence
nodes.abstract: Abstract The popularization of multi-camera systems and multi-view image capture has led to the emergence of sparse multi-view image super-resolution (MVSR) as a promising research direction. The primary approach to sparse multi-view super-resolution (SR) currently involves extending traditional single-view SR and stereo SR frameworks, i.e., extracting features from each view and performing pixel-domain alignment and fusion to leverage cross-view reference information. However, this straightforward framework has two main drawbacks. First, performing cross-view fusion in the pixel domain disregards the spatial perception information that multi-view images provide. Second, feature alignment and fusion across views introduce considerable redundant and repetitive computations, which hinders further scalability to more viewpoints. This paper proposes a novel sparse multi-view SR framework based on a unified spatial representation reference. Specifically, the proposed method first computes a multi-plane image spatial representation from the multi-view images. This multi-plane image (MPI) representation encapsulates all the information from each view and has spatial perception. Subsequently, an upsampled reference image is rendered from the MPI representation for the low-resolution views. A high-low frequency separation fusion network is then proposed to upscale the input low-resolution images based on the rendered reference. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for recovering high-frequency details.

nodes.name: Pareto-based parameter screening for mid- and high-spatial-frequency errors in CO <sub>2</sub> laser beam figuring of fused silica
nodes.venue: Applied Optics
nodes.abstract: Laser beam figuring (LBF) with microsecond-pulsed CO 2 laser radiation enables nanometer-precision material removal on fused silica for deterministic surface figure correction in high-performance optical fabrication. This work presents a framework combining experimentally measured single-pulse craters with a geometric line-synthesis model to construct geometric reference topographies under a pulse-independent-kernel assumption as a function of pulse duration t p and pulse spacing d x . A Pareto-dominance analysis of 60 parameter combinations quantifies the trade-off between mid-spatial-frequency (MSFE) and high-spatial-frequency (HSFE) roughness over a bounded synthesis window, where it arises from the line terminations. Within the investigated parameter space, equal weighting selects t p =90µs and d x =5−10µm for a single pass ( R q MSFE =6.17−6.40nm, R q HSFE =1.06−1.34nm). A limited experimental comparison at two pulse spacings shows substantial deviations from the geometric reference model at high overlap. At equal weighting, the measured lines favor the larger of the two pitches. A transient thermal simulation indicates interpulse heat accumulation. The reported optimum is therefore a property of the defined synthesis construction rather than a validated prediction of fabricated surfaces.

An Intelligent Deep Learning Framework for Cardiac Arrhythmia Detection and Risk Prediction
nodes.abstract: Abstract Cardiac Arrhythmia detection using continuous ECG monitoring is challenging because abnormal heartbeats occur irregularly, and their patterns may vary from one person to another. ECG signals can also contain noise caused by body movements, muscle activity, and baseline variations, which can affect the accuracy of detection. To address these challenges, this project proposes an intelligent deep learning framework that combines a 1D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) network, and an Attention Mechanism to detect and classify heartbeats into five AAMI classes. The CNN extracts important features from ECG signals, while the BiLSTM learns the sequential patterns of heartbeats. The CNN extracts important features from ECG signals, particularly the QRS complex, while reducing the influence of less relevant information and noise. To improve the interpretability of the results, a gradient-based Explainable AI (XAI) method is used to generate saliency heatmaps that highlight important regions of the ECG signals. The framework also includes a risk stratification module that categorizes detected cases into low, medium, and high-risk levels based on predefined criteria. The proposed model is evaluated using the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database, with ECG signals segmented into 0.6 second windows around the R-peaks. The target is to achieve high classification accuracy while providing understandable results and useful risk information. This framework aims to support continuous ECG monitoring and assist healthcare professionals in identifying abnormal heartbeat more efficiently.
